# Exact obstruction to a log-concave shadow in one integer fiber

The following proposed strengthening of OC is false, already for n=d=1:

> There exists an integer fiber carrying a log-concave probability
> measure nu such that nu(H)<=2 mu(H) for every closed ambient halfspace,
> where mu is normalized mixed-integer volume.

This note excludes every log-concave density and also every point mass.
It does not refute OC, which requires only a sufficiently deep point.

## The convex body and its integer marginal

Let

    C=conv{(0,0),(4,0),(2,61/20),(0,2)}.

This is a compact full-dimensional convex quadrilateral. Its integer
fibers are

    C_0=[0,2],
    C_1=[0,101/40],
    C_2=[0,61/20],
    C_3=[0,61/40],
    C_4={0}.

The first three upper endpoints are collinear, as are the last three,
and all lower endpoints are zero. These formulas therefore follow
directly from the polygon's two upper edges. The total intrinsic
one-dimensional mixed measure is

    M=(80+101+122+61)/40=91/10.

Any target probability supported in a fiber k and dominated on every
halfspace by twice mu requires k to be a weighted median. A vertical
containing halfspace has target probability one and must have mu-mass
at least one half. Here the only possible fiber is k=2:

    mass(z<=0)=80/40<M/2,
    mass(z<=1)=181/40<182/40=M/2,
    mass(z>=3)=61/40<M/2,
    mass(z>=4)=0.

Thus any such target must be supported in [0,61/20] in fiber 2.

## Two exact ambient cap constraints

Consider the closed halfspaces

    H_R={x>=-z/2+121/40},
    H_L={x<=4z-437/80}.

The first captures lengths 0,0,41/40,0 in positive fibers 0,1,2,3.
Its target-fiber threshold is 81/40. The second captures lengths
0,0,203/80,61/40 and has target-fiber threshold 203/80.
Consequently any dominated target probability nu satisfies

    nu([81/40,infinity)) <= 2(41/40)/M = 41/182 =: q,
    nu((203/80,infinity)) >= 1-2(325/80)/M = 39/364 =: B.

For a density, the strict and weak endpoint choices coincide. A point
mass is immediately impossible: positive mass above 203/80 would put
all its mass above 81/40, contradicting q<1. A point mass at 203/80
already violates the H_L constraint.

## Lemma: equal-interval masses of a log-concave density

Let f be a nonnegative log-concave density on the line and let I_j be
successive intervals of a fixed length h>0. Put m_j=integral_{I_j} f.
Then

    m_{j+1}^2>=m_j m_{j+2}.

The positive m_j occur consecutively. In particular, where the masses
are positive, the ratios m_j/m_{j+1} are nondecreasing with j.

Proof. For x<=y and h>0, log-concavity gives

    f(x+h)f(y)>=f(x)f(y+h).

If the right side is zero this is immediate. Otherwise all four points
are in the positive interval of f. The two inner points x+h,y have the
same sum as the outer points x,y+h. Applying log-concavity to the two
convex combinations with complementary coefficients and multiplying
proves the inequality. Integrate it over x in I_j and y in I_{j+1}.
The left integral is m_{j+1}^2 and the right integral is m_jm_{j+2}.
Consecutiveness follows because {f>0} is an interval. QED.

## The contradiction for every log-concave density

Partition [-1/40,61/20] into six intervals I_0,...,I_5 of equal length

    h=41/80.

Their union contains the whole possible support [0,61/20]. The last
two intervals have union [81/40,61/20], and the last interval is
[203/80,61/20]. The two cap constraints therefore imply

    m_4+m_5<=q=41/182,
    m_5>=B=39/364,
    m_4<=q-B=43/364=:A.

Because q<1 and m_5>0, some earlier interval also has positive mass;
consecutiveness forces m_4>0. By the ratio inequality in the lemma,

    m_j/m_{j+1}<=m_4/m_5<=A/B=43/39

for every earlier positive pair. Earlier zero masses only strengthen
the following bounds. Thus

    m_3<=A^2/B,
    m_2<=A^3/B^2,
    m_1<=A^4/B^3,
    m_0<=A^5/B^4.

Adding and using the bound on the last two intervals yields

    1=sum_{j=0}^5 m_j
      <=q+sum_{j=2}^5 A^j/B^(j-1)
      =50046773/60149466
      =1-10102693/60149466<1,

a contradiction. All constants and cap masses are verified with exact
rational arithmetic by verify_logconcave_shadow_obstruction.py.

One can avoid the larger rational number using the looser estimates
q<1/4, A<1/8, A/B<10/9, which give

    sum m_j < 1/4+(1/8)sum_{k=1}^4(10/9)^k
            =5939/6561<1.

Hence there is no log-concave shadow in any integer fiber. In particular
neither exponential-family targets nor arbitrary optimized log-concave
targets provide a universal domination mechanism with factor two.

## Why the earlier CDF screen missed the obstruction

Log-concavity of a density implies concavity of both log F and
log(1-F), but those conditions alone are weaker. The contradiction here
uses the ratios of successive interval masses, which depend on
increments of F rather than F and its survival function separately.
It also combines a bound on the LAST TWO bins with a lower bound on
the LAST bin, then propagates the resulting ratio across all earlier
bins. Testing only independent three-bin lower/upper bounds can miss
this cumulative incompatibility.

The ordinary log-concave optimal-depth theorem in
candidate 0f025bdf9a51573b remains valid. The failed ingredient is the
existence of such a target shadow for arbitrary mixed-integer bodies.
